# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 3
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 3

---

*[THE PALACE THAT WASN'T — AND WAS.]*

1. After the wedding, Abbanes brought Thomas before King Gundaphorus. "My lord," he said, "I found what you needed — a carpenter and a builder, exactly as you ordered."

2. The king was pleased. He looked Thomas over. "What can you do?" he asked. "Can you build me a palace?"

3. "That's exactly what I do," Thomas said. "That's why I'm here."

4. The king took him outside the city. They walked a long way until the king stopped and pointed at an expanse of open land. "Here," he said. "I want my palace here."

5. Thomas looked at the land. "I'll build it," he said. "And it will be something to behold."

6. "When do you start?"

7. "Now," Thomas said. "And I'll see it through to the end."

8. The king was generous. He ordered that Thomas should have access to the treasury — gold and silver and everything else he needed. Then the king left for another country.

9. The moment the king was gone, Thomas took all the gold and silver and set out through the villages and cities. He gave it all away. To the poor. To the sick. He clothed people who had nothing. "The king commissioned me to build him a palace," he told everyone. "And I am building him one."

10. He kept on doing this for a long time.

11. Eventually the king sent a messenger back to check on the palace. What was the progress? He wanted news.

12. The messenger found Thomas and asked about the palace.

13. "Nearly done," Thomas said. "Finished, actually — just waiting on the roof."

14. The king was delighted when he heard this.

---
*PNEUMA note: Thomas's answer "I am building him one" (v.9) is magnificent in its double meaning. He is building a palace — but not of stone. The roof (v.13) refers to the final act of consecration, when the palace of heaven would be sealed. The king's delight (v.14) is darkly ironic: he is about to discover he commissioned the wrong kind of palace entirely.*
